briefs.polymarket-7150180: The question is whether the Binance BTC/USDT 1-minute candle closing at 12:00 ET (17:00 UTC) on 2026-11-25 has a close above $56,000; exactly 56,000 is No. Binance BTCUSDT read 61,799 to 61,810 at 10:13-10:14 UTC on 2026-11-20 (https://api.binance.com/api/v3/ticker/price?symbol=BTCUSDT), so the threshold is 9.4% below spot. Daily closes fell from 84,093 on 2026-10-21 to 61,987 on 2026-11-19, with 63,068 on 2026-11-18 (https://api.binance.com/api/v3/klines?symbol=BTCUSDT&interval=1d&limit=31). The standard deviation of daily log returns over the last 29 returns was 2.28%, which gives about 5.1% over five days, so the threshold sits near 1.9 standard deviations away on a thin-tailed model. In 1,995 overlapping 5-day windows since 2021-05-31, the close five days later was above 0.906 times the start in 95.2% of cases, though the windows overlap and use daily closes. This time the drawdown is steep: month-to-date declines of 16-23% (https://cryptobriefing.com/bitcoin-falls-23-november-2026-bear-market/, 2026-11-17) and US spot ETF outflows of $1.07B in the week of Nov 9-13 and $2.35B for November through nine trading days (https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-11-14-bitcoin-etfs-lose-1-billion-for-the-second-week-in-a-row-as-crypto-funds-except-one-440337, 2026-11-14). The next FOMC meeting is Dec 8-9, and the BLS lists no releases between Nov 21 and Nov 25 (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm), so no scheduled macro catalyst falls in the window. Trade press names Fed expectations, ETF outflows and leveraged longs as unresolved risks to the $60,000 level (https://cryptoticker.io/en/bitcoin-price-62000-crash-fed-hike-60000-level-november-15-2026/, 2026-11-15). A weekly drop of 16% occurred just days ago, so a further 9.4% fall is within recent experience. The answer would move toward No on a break below 58,000 with renewed liquidations or large ETF outflows, and toward Yes if price stabilizes above 60,000 through the weekend. The single-pair, single-candle settlement rule adds small noise.
